reviews.review_text:
Yesbeauty
4 contributions
0
Special delicacy worth to try, freshly prepared.
Sep 2019 • Family
Awesome to see how the snake had what it was deserved, to become a big banquet: two (red & green, freshly drained from snake) alcoholic drinks, beating heart sashimi, three soups plus around six courses. Fortunately, this country is not my country (protects most sorts of dangerous animals which do not protect human), the snakes have their fair chance to serve us as if chickens & ducks.
Just chose the snake, watched the skilful staff played with it & made it toothless. Then its head was hit hard and treated humanely in unconscious.
No need to see the menu to order because it is always a set package, from skin to bones. They sell per snake, instead of part of snake or per dish. It maybe too much food for solo or couple travellers, so they may join or bring take away boxes.
'Turtle' in the menu was a wrong translation, it should be 'pigeon'.
Worth it! VND1.2 million for four people. Thus, the cost for each person was just like a few bowls of noodles. Heavier cobra was VND1.8 million.
The English level of the staff or translation mistakes (menu) were minor issues, because the price was correct.
We were so full & a bit drunk.
In South East Asia, usually the restaurants do NOT serve bottled water for free. Here, customers can return the unused wet tissue &/or bottled water.
By online transport app, one way (car) from Old Quarter is around VND100K. Motorcycle is cheaper. *VND23150 is one USD.

Worst culinary experience
Dec 2019
We came to this restaurant following recommendation of our local tour guide whom we spent half the day with, driving around the city. We hoped for vibrant place where we could experience snake show and this was promised to us for “only” 60 usd (for 2 people). When we arrived for the dinner, the place was empty, staff completely disorganized with no English whatsoever. We have not been given a menu so couldn’t order for ourself, not we could see the prices. All dishes where ordered by our guide, and all tasted really bad. Service was extremely slow, despite lack of other customers we had to wave at them few times to come and fill up our drinks or clear the table. We thought we will be able to see live snakes however this has not happened, and eventually we left the place hungry. We felt almost robbed by our tour guide, who not only had a feast at our cost (he sat with us the entire dinner and finished all meals ordered), but surely has also earned money for bringing us to this place. Overall worst culinary experience

An experience we won't forget
Feb 2016 • Friends
This restaurant was recommended by our hotel. We asked about some of the others and we were told this is where the locals go.

Our hotel arranged for a taxi. It cost about $120k dong from old quarter. It was dark when we arrived and there was little street lighting. The road and alleys were narrow. It made my friend very nervous about getting out of the cab and the concern that we may not find a taxi back. The restaurant was about 50 meter walk from the street and the sign was hard to see.

Once we stepped inside, things happened very fast. Language and communication was a challenge but we figured it out. Ordered a cobra and watched. We were then seated. We were the only westerners in the restaurant. 

The courses were brought out and we found most to be better than expected. We actually finished off a lot of the dishes and drinks. The best part was when we were invited to the table of some locals to do shots in celebration of the new year. It was an awesome experience and a kind gesture.

The language barrier and service level could be an issue for some. Come here for the experience, not for 5 star service.

The restaurant arranged for our return taxi and we arrived back at our hotel without incident.

A unique and genuine food experience
Dec 2015 • Friends
The location is far from the center of the city, but its worth the trip for this authentic experience. In spite of the few negative reviews inaccuratly dismissing this as a touristy place, this is a truly northern Vietnamese experience. Our table was a mix of locals and expats, but beyond that, there were only locals eating here. We ate a decent size cobra that cost about 2milVND (about $90). It was turned into 8 courses for the 4 of us. Not to mention the alcohol mixed with the blood and the bile. 
Maybe not for the faint of heart, but for those seeking a local food adventure, it is a must.

Fantastic experience and dinner.
Oct 2014 • Friends
This is not a restaurant for the faint of heart. 
You choose a snake, either a bamboo snake or a cobra. A cobra costs about a million VND (£17).
The snake is butchered in front of you and the still-beating heart is put into a glass of vodka for the bravest to down.
The snake makes loads of dishes or all kinds that will feed up 4 people. So feeding 4 people for £17 was pretty good, and it turns out that snake is delicious!

I loved it as a meal and an experience.

Not for the Faint of Heart!
Dec 2014 • Couples
My boyfriend and I were visiting Hanoi, and heard about the snake restaurants. Given the fact that we were on an adventure to try new food, we couldn't pass it up! I will keep my review short and sweet...

We were so glad we tried it. The food was amazing, and very reasonably priced for what you get! They prepared the snake 8 different ways for us. They do go through their ritual and kill the snake right in front of you, and cut off it's head and rip out the heart! As for service, it was about the same as the other restaurants we went to in Vietnam. Nothing to write home about, but it wasn't bad either. Bottom line, I would highly recommend going. It's a unique experience!
